scope: Injected independent-array PLY-3 restore trace of decoder staging-buffer release; no production code change.
method: An isolated server disabled numeric-array reuse and applied the fractional-seed allocation diagnostic. It instrumented the existing per-buffer release condition in the served bundle and forwarded only buffer sizes, eligibility, reference count and post-transfer length to the test log. The full original scan was split, exported, downloaded and selected for GUI reopen under the 4 GiB/25% CPU guard.
observation: Each of the four buffers was eligible for release, had one numeric entry, was not protected by a graph alias, and reported zero byteLength after ArrayBuffer.transfer(0). The GUI reported the project imported, but the first post-reopen MCP geometry digest timed out; geometry and history were not verified.
limitations: Detachment proves the JavaScript views were detached, not when the operating system reclaimed physical memory.
The injected and instrumented workload does not prove production timing, general resource behavior, or a successful independent restore.
The restore ownership, native comparison and M2 closure gates remain open.
